data.description: Domain ownership — the strongest item on the rival's decoupling menu for divergent standards, since an owner both sets and meets the standard — inherits the account's own churn objection: a domain bound to an owner can fail the way a rota bound to days does when the owner's shifts explode, and swap-on-request reintroduces the micro-agreements it was meant to escape. If the menu is opened, domains need scheduled swap review; until then this is unresolved.
